title: Worship God
catalogue_audience: Shared instruction or study teaching. Read the original audience, conditions and existing classification before applying it.
context_note: Original recipient: John, corrected by the angel. Record type: Direct instruction; continuity review open. The angel refuses John’s worship and directs him to God. This concerns the object of worship; the messenger’s role does not make the messenger divine. The parallel scene gives the same direction to John and provides its own rationale concerning the testimony of Jesus. Link both source scenes on the existing worship record.
origin_basis: An angel in Revelation’s vision tells John to worship God. The angel is a messenger and redirects worship away from himself.

additional_scripture.context_note: The correction parallels 22:9, already indexed as X012. The reason given in 19:10 refers to the testimony of Jesus.

title: Do not seal up the prophecy of this scroll
catalogue_audience: John
context_note: The command states that the time is near. It is distinct from the direction to seal the thunders at 10:4.
origin_basis: Speaker or source in this passage: The angel who has been speaking with John.
speaker_or_source: The angel who has been speaking with John
original_audience_audit: John

title: The righteous and holy are called to continue as the time draws near
catalogue_audience: The hearers described as righteous, holy, wrongdoers and filthy
context_note: The four parallel clauses distinguish paths of wrongdoing and righteousness in the closing warning. The opening clauses portray continued wrongdoing as the counterpart to righteous persistence.
origin_basis: Verse 11 continues the angel’s words to John that begin in verse 10.
speaker_or_source: The angel continuing the closing charge to John
original_audience_audit: The hearers described as righteous, holy, wrongdoers and filthy

title: Those who wash their robes are blessed with access to the city
catalogue_audience: Those who hear the blessing and the contrasting warning
context_note: The Saints text commends those who wash their robes by describing access to the tree of life and the city. The contrast with those outside supplies the warning.
origin_basis: Speaker or source in this passage: The voice of the closing vision, unnamed in these verses.
speaker_or_source: The voice of the closing vision, unnamed in these verses
original_audience_audit: Those who hear the blessing and the contrasting warning

additional_scripture.context_note: The elder explains the earlier vision of the people who washed their robes in the blood of the Lamb.

title: Jesus sends His angel to testify for the churches
catalogue_audience: His angel, with the churches receiving the testimony
context_note: Jesus identifies Himself and explicitly reports sending His angel to testify. The opening and closing scenes distinguish this assignment from John’s own instruction to write and send what he saw.
origin_basis: Speaker or source in this passage: Jesus.
original_audience_audit: His angel, with the churches receiving the testimony

additional_scripture.context_note: The prologue traces the revelation from God through Jesus and His angel to John.
The angel reports being sent to show God’s servants what must take place soon.

title: Invite the thirsty to take the water of life freely
catalogue_audience: Hearers, those who thirst and those who desire the water
context_note: The verse records who says Come and distinguishes the call to echo it from the invitation to receive.
origin_basis: The invitation begins with the Spirit and the bride. The passage then calls on hearers to echo it and invites the thirsty to receive the water of life.
speaker_or_source: The Spirit and bride begin the invitation; the hearer is called to echo it
original_audience_audit: Hearers, those who thirst and those who desire the water

title: Preserve the words of this prophecy without addition or removal
catalogue_audience: Everyone who hears the words of the prophecy of the scroll
context_note: The two conditions refer expressly to the prophecy of this scroll and state corresponding consequences.
origin_basis: The testifying voice in the epilogue gives the conditional warnings. These verses do not name the speaker explicitly.
speaker_or_source: The speaker testifying in the epilogue
original_audience_audit: Everyone who hears the words of the prophecy of the scroll
